s: Which one of the following was the difference between Bhakti devotion and formal Sufi religious practice?
o: Bhakti rejected personal devotion, whereas Sufism confined worship to idol rituals.
Bhakti emphasised Vedic ritual, whereas Sufism rejected all forms of devotion.
Bhakti stressed devotion over Vedic ritual, while Sufism valued inner experience over formal Shariat.
Both movements exclusively supported priestly authority and formal ritual.
x: Bhakti traditions placed devotion above Vedic ritual and priestly mediation, while Sufism emphasised inner spiritual experience rather than merely formal observance of the Shariat.

s: Which of the following was NOT shared by the Bhakti and Sufi traditions?
x: Both valued the guide-disciple bond, devotion over ritual and vernacular preaching; exclusive idol worship was not common to them.

s: Whose rigid orthodoxy did Kabir and Nanak criticise?
x: Kabir and Nanak criticised the orthodoxies of both Hinduism and Islam and stressed spiritual equality.

s: What did the interaction between Bhakti and Sufi traditions lead to?
x: Bhakti-Sufi interaction produced a composite Indo-Islamic culture, with shrines and vernacular traditions acting as shared spaces.

s: Amir Khusrau, the disciple of Nizamuddin Auliya, introduced which element of Qawwali?
o: Fana, the final stage of spiritual union
x: Amir Khusrau introduced Qaul, the opening hymn of Qawwali.

s: Which one of the following Sufi orders was opposed to musical practices such as sama?
x: The Naqshbandis opposed sama and associated musical practices, in contrast to the Chishti and Suhrawardi traditions mentioned in this context.

s: Who introduced the Qaul, associated with the early development of qawwali?
x: Amir Khusrau is credited with introducing the Qaul, which became associated with qawwali traditions around Sufi shrines.

s: Which music tradition remained closely tied to temple Bhakti?
x: Carnatic music remained linked with temple Bhakti, while Hindustani absorbed Persian, Bhakti and Sufi influences.

s: In medieval India, many Sanskrit works on music were translated into which language?
x: Many Sanskrit musical works were rendered into Persian; the early Chishtis too were fond of music.

s: With which ruler is Lahjat-i-Sikandar Shahi, a Persian rendering of Sanskrit music works, linked?
x: Lahjat-i-Sikandar Shahi is associated with Sikandar Lodi.

s: To which year does Ghunyat-ul-Munya, a Persian work on music, date?
x: Ghunyat-ul-Munya dates to 1375.

s: With whom is the Melakarta raga system associated?
x: Venkatamakhin is linked with the Melakarta raga system; Shyama Shastri was a Carnatic composer.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the interaction between Nath yogis and Sufis?
o: Hath-yogic techniques influenced some Sufi practices
It was confined exclusively to temple rituals
Sufis adopted certain yogic meditation practices
x: The interaction involved dialogues, meditation and breath control; it was not confined to temple rituals.

s: Which Sufi equated 'Alakh Niranjan' with 'Khuda' in Hindi verse?
x: Hamiduddin Nagori equated the Nath term 'Alakh Niranjan' with 'Khuda' in Hindi verse. Nizamuddin Auliya noted the yogic Siva-Sakti division of the body, Ahmad Sirhindi was an orthodox Naqshbandi, and Bahauddin Zakariya was a Suhrawardi close to the court.

s: The Nathpanthi tradition of Hath Yoga is particularly associated with which of the following figures?
x: The Kanphata Yogis followed the Nath tradition of Gorakhnath and were practitioners of Hath Yoga.

s: Which one of the following statements about Nizamuddin Auliya and yogic ideas is correct?
o: He was struck by the yogic division of the body into Siva and Sakti.
He founded the Nathpanthi order at Ajmer.
He rejected all knowledge of Nath yogic practices.
He translated Amritakund into Persian during the 13th century.
x: Nizamuddin Auliya noted the yogic division of the body: Siva from the head to the navel and Sakti below the navel.

s: Who practised Hath Yoga, whose techniques some Sufis adopted?
x: Hath Yoga was practised by the Nathpanthi yogis of Gorakhnath's tradition, and Sufis adopted techniques such as breath control.

s: Which Sufi order did NOT adopt yogic breath control?
x: After the Amritakund was translated, breath control was adopted in all orders except the Naqshbandis.

s: Which Hath-yogic text was translated into Arabic and Persian in the 13th century?
x: The Amritakund, a Hath-yogic text, was rendered into Arabic and Persian in the 13th century.

s: To whom is the Nathpanth tradition traced?
x: The Nathpanth goes back to Matsyendranath; Gorakhnath and the Kanphata yogis practised Hath Yoga.

s: Which of the following was a social impact of the Bhakti and Sufi movements?
o: They closed khanqahs to lower social groups
They weakened priestly and Brahmanical dominance
x: The movements weakened priestly dominance and khanqahs welcomed different groups, but caste was not completely abolished.

s: What did the Rishi movement of Kashmir emphasise?
o: Universal love, service to all castes and vegetarianism
Courtly luxury, military conquest and Persianisation
Purdah, child marriage and priestly monopoly
Caste exclusiveness, animal sacrifice and compulsory meat-eating
x: The Rishi movement served all castes, emphasised universal love and adopted vegetarianism, although the Shariat permitted meat.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with the occupational or caste background of the saint?
x: Namdev belonged to a tailor family. Kabir was a weaver, Ravidas a leather tanner or shoemaker, Sena a barber and Dhanna a Jat cultivator.

s: Veerashaivism associated with Basava advocated which one of the following combinations?
o: Vedic ritualism, animal sacrifice and purdah
Caste hierarchy, child marriage and widow seclusion
Priestly monopoly, child marriage and caste exclusiveness
Caste opposition, widow remarriage and gender equality
x: Basava’s Veerashaivism condemned caste and child marriage and supported widow remarriage and gender equality.

s: Which Andhra saint had disciples like Siddayya (a Dudekula) and Kakkaiah (a Madiga)?
x: Veerabrahmam's disciples cut across castes and he admitted women; he opposed untouchability and idol worship.

s: Who is regarded as the first medieval reformer to denounce caste outright, with disciples such as Kabir, Raidas, Sena and Dhanna?
x: Ramananda was the first medieval reformer to denounce caste outright; his disciples included Kabir (weaver), Raidas (shoemaker), Sena (barber) and Dhanna (Jat cultivator). Ramanuja preached Vishishtadvaita, Basavanna led Veerashaivism, and Chaitanya is linked with sankirtan; none had this group of disciples.

s: Which statement about women in the Bhakti and Sufi movements is correct?
o: Women were excluded from spiritual expression in both
Only royal women could express spirituality publicly
The movements gave women room for open spiritual expression
Women were admitted to Sufi orders but to no Bhakti order
x: Both movements created space for women's open spiritual expression; Veerabrahmam also admitted women to his order.

s: Which of the following pairs of traditions formed part of the pre-colonial social-reform line in Andhra?
x: The Andhra pre-colonial reform line included Veerashaivism and Srivaishnavism, along with figures such as Brahmanayudu, Vemana, Veerabrahmam and Nasaraiah.

s: With whom is Chapakudu, the practice of inter-dining in Palnadu, associated?
x: Brahmanaidu of Palnadu promoted Chapakudu inter-dining; his commander Karnamadasu was an untouchable.

s: Nasaraiah, a Sayyid reformer who opposed untouchability, worked among the Madigas of which place?
x: Nasaraiah worked among the Madigas of Vinukonda.

s: Which of the following pairs (saint – occupational background) is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: Kabir was a weaver; Dhanna was the Jat cultivator.

s: With which of the following is Lal Ded, also known as Lalla, associated?
o: Kashmir and the inspiration of the Rishi movement
Tamil Nadu and the Alvar tradition
Andhra and the composition of Molla Ramayanam
x: Lal Ded or Lalla belonged to Kashmir and inspired the Rishi movement.

s: Which of the following groups consists entirely of women associated with open expression of devotion?
o: Mirabai, Andal, Lal Ded, Janabai and Bahinabai
Andal, Kabir, Janabai, Bahinabai and Lal Ded
Mirabai, Ravidas, Andal, Janabai and Bahinabai
Mirabai, Surdas, Andal, Lal Ded and Janabai
x: Mirabai, Andal, Lal Ded, Janabai and Bahinabai are the women named for expressing their devotion openly.

s: For which work is Molla, a woman saint-poet, known?
x: Molla is known for the Molla Ramayanam.

s: Which of the following was NOT a woman associated with the Bhakti movement?
x: Dhanna was a Jat cultivator saint; Andal, Janabai and Bahinabai are among the women saints.

s: Besides Kabir, Nanak and Ravidas, who among the following belonged to the Sant tradition, which blended Hindu and Islamic ideas?
x: The Kabirpanth and Sant tradition included Kabir, Nanak, Ravidas and Dadu and blended Hindu and Islamic ideas.

s: Who carried forward the syncretic tradition of Akbar's Sulh-i-kul and Din-i-Ilahi?
x: Dara Shikoh carried the syncretic tradition forward, while Ahmad Sirhindi attacked these policies.

s: With which movement is Sheikh Nuruddin associated?
x: Sheikh Nuruddin is associated with the Rishi movement; Basaveswara led the Lingayat/Veerasaiva tradition.

s: With whom are the early feelings of national awakening among the Marathas through the Bhakti movement linked?
o: Kabir, Dadu Dayal and Guru Nanak
x: Among the Marathas, early national awakening was associated with Tukaram, Ramdas and Shivaji.

s: With which region is the Rishi movement associated?
x: The Rishi movement belongs to Kashmir; Dadupanth to Rajasthan and Mahanubhava to Maharashtra.

s: Which of the following pairs (followers – tradition) is correctly matched?
x: Basava's followers are the Lingayats; Lakulisha founded Pashupata Shaivism, Matsyendranath the Nathpanth, and Guru Nanak's followers are Sikhs.

s: Who founded the Mahanubhava sect of Maharashtra?
x: The Mahanubhava sect was founded by Chakradhar Swami in Maharashtra.

s: The Dadupanth arose in which region?
x: Dadupanth was founded by Dadu in Rajasthan.

s: In which year was Akbar's Din-i-Ilahi promulgated?
x: Akbar launched Din-i-Ilahi in 1582.

s: Dara Shikoh, who continued Akbar's syncretic line, belonged to which Sufi order?
x: Dara Shikoh was a Qadiri; Sirhindi, a Naqshbandi, attacked the syncretic line.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
x: Jnaneshwari was composed by Jnaneshwar in Marathi. Kaalagnanam was composed by Potuluri Veerabrahmam, while the other two pairs have incorrect authors and languages.

s: Who among the following used satire in common Telugu to criticise birth-based inequality?
x: Vemana, associated with the seventeenth century, used satire in common Telugu against birth-based inequality.

s: With whom is Kaalagnanam in Telugu associated?
x: Kaalagnanam is by Veerabrahmam; Vemana wrote 17th-century satire on birth inequality.

s: With the growth of literature in which language is Amir Khusrau associated?
x: Amir Khusrau is linked with Urdu and Hindavi.

s: The Jnaneshwari belongs to the literature of which language?
x: The Jnaneshwari is a Marathi work; Bengali is associated with Padavali kirtans.

s: Padavali kirtans enriched the literature of which language?
x: Padavali kirtans, linked with Chaitanya's sankirtan, are part of Bengali Bhakti literature.

s: Which one of the following developments represents the later limitation of the Bhakti and Sufi movements?
o: The movements became confined only to royal courts.
Vernacular devotional traditions were entirely abandoned.
Their traditions hardened into separate sects and panths.
x: The movements later hardened into separate sects and panths, despite their earlier emphasis on broad spiritual and social interaction.

s: Which of the following continued despite the Bhakti and Sufi movements?
x: The movements did not end purdah or restrictions on women's public life, and caste inequalities persisted.

s: What was a limitation of Srivaishnavism and Veerashaivism?
o: They made caste inequality their principal objective
They had no concern with social reform
They ended every form of social discrimination
They opposed caste, but caste inequalities could not be eradicated
x: Although Srivaishnavism and Veerashaivism sought to reduce caste differences, caste inequalities persisted.

s:
Consider the following statements about the limitations of the Bhakti and Sufi movements:
1. Caste persisted.
2. Purdah continued.
3. The sects remained free of sectarian hardening.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Caste persisted and purdah stayed, but the sects hardened over time, so statement 3 is false.

s: Which work was written by Guru Gobind Singh, who fought 14 wars against Aurangzeb's forces?
x: Guru Gobind Singh wrote the Zafarnama, which advocated the sword only when all other avenues failed.

s: The Chali Mukte are associated with which event?
o: The release of Guru Hargobind from Gwalior Fort
The founding of the Khalsa at Anandpur
The compilation of the Adi Granth at Amritsar
The defence of Guru Gobind Singh at Muktsar
x: The Chali Mukte, or 40 liberated ones, died defending Guru Gobind Singh at Muktsar; the event is commemorated as Maghi.

s: In which year did Guru Gobind Singh found the Khalsa on Baisakhi day?
x: Guru Gobind Singh founded the Khalsa on 13 April 1699 (Baisakhi) with the Panj Pyaras. 1675 is Guru Tegh Bahadur's martyrdom, and 1710 is Banda Singh Bahadur's conquest of Sirhind; 1704 is not the Khalsa's date.

s: After the death of Guru Gobind Singh, to whom did the Guruship pass permanently?
x: After Guru Gobind Singh, the Guru Granth Sahib was declared the eternal Guru.

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the Five Ks of the Khalsa?
x: The Five Ks are Kesh, Kangha, Kara, Kachera and Kirpan; Kirtan is not one of them.

s: What are the first five volunteers baptised into the Khalsa known as?
x: The Panj Pyare were the five volunteers baptised with sacred nectar.

s: Who wrote the Zafarnama, a letter accusing the Mughals of betrayal?
x: Guru Gobind Singh wrote the Zafarnama accusing the Mughals of betrayal.

s: Where was the Khalsa founded on 13 April 1699?
x: Guru Gobind Singh founded the Khalsa on Baisakhi, 13 April 1699, at Takht Keshgarh Sahib in Anandpur.

s: What was Ranjit Singh's high court at Lahore called?
x: His high court was the Adalat-i-Ala; the Dal Khalsa was the combined force of the misls.

s: In which year did Ranjit Singh capture Lahore, which became the capital of his kingdom?
x: Ranjit Singh captured Lahore in 1799 and made it his capital.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Treaty of Amritsar:
1. It was concluded in 1809 with Lord Minto.
2. It fixed the Sutlej as the boundary between the British and Ranjit Singh's territories.
3. It fixed the Ravi as the boundary between the British and Ranjit Singh's territories.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Treaty of Amritsar (1809, with Lord Minto) fixed the Sutlej, not the Ravi, as the boundary.

s: From whom did Ranjit Singh obtain the Kohinoor diamond in 1813?
x: Ranjit Singh obtained the Kohinoor from the Afghan ruler Shah Shuja in 1813. Lord Minto signed the Treaty of Amritsar (1809) with him, and Duleep Singh was his last successor. Nadir Shah took the Kohinoor from Delhi in 1739, long before 1813.

s: Where was Maharaja Ranjit Singh born in 1780?
x: Ranjit Singh was born on 13 November 1780 at Gujranwala.

s: Maha Singh, the father of Ranjit Singh, was the chief of which misl?
x: Ranjit Singh's father Maha Singh headed the Sukerchakia misl.

s: Who was called the 'Lion of Punjab'?
x: Maharaja Ranjit Singh of the Sukerchakia misl was called the Lion of Punjab.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Sis Ganj — Cremation place of Guru Tegh Bahadur
Rakab Ganj — Execution place of Guru Tegh Bahadur
Sis Ganj — Execution place of Guru Tegh Bahadur
Muktsar — Execution place of Guru Tegh Bahadur
x: Sis Ganj marks the execution place of Guru Tegh Bahadur, while Rakab Ganj marks his cremation place.

s: In which year was Guru Tegh Bahadur executed by Aurangzeb at Chandni Chowk, Delhi?
x: Guru Tegh Bahadur was executed at Chandni Chowk in Delhi in 1675 by order of Aurangzeb.

s: Who is regarded as the first martyr Guru of the Sikhs?
x: Guru Arjan Dev is regarded as the first martyr Guru.

s: Which of the following statements regarding Guru Hargobind is correct?
o: He introduced the Gurmukhi script and founded Ramdaspur.
He militarised the Panth and was released from Gwalior Fort in 1619 with 52 prisoners.
He founded the Khalsa at Anandpur Sahib in 1699.
He compiled the Adi Granth and became its first martyr.
x: Guru Hargobind militarised the Panth and was released from Gwalior Fort in 1619 along with 52 prisoners, an event associated with Bandi Chhor Divas.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Guru Arjan Dev – Established the Khalsa Panth
Guru Hargobind – Compiled the Adi Granth
Guru Tegh Bahadur – Executed by Aurangzeb in 1675
Guru Gobind Singh – Executed by Aurangzeb in 1675
x: Guru Tegh Bahadur was executed by Aurangzeb in 1675; Guru Arjan compiled the Adi Granth, Guru Hargobind began the military tradition and Guru Gobind Singh founded the Khalsa.

s: Bandi Chhor Divas commemorates the release of which Sikh Guru from Gwalior Fort (1619)?
x: Guru Hargobind was released from Gwalior Fort in 1619 with 52 prisoners, marked as Bandi Chhor Divas.

s: Which Sikh Guru is called 'Hind-di-Chadar'?
x: Guru Tegh Bahadur, executed by Aurangzeb at Delhi in 1675, is called Hind-di-Chadar.

s: Guru Arjan Dev was executed in 1606 under which Mughal emperor?
x: Arjan Dev was executed under Jahangir in 1606; Tegh Bahadur under Aurangzeb.

s: Guru Arjan Dev was charged with supporting which rebel prince?
x: Jahangir executed Arjan Dev for supporting the rebel Prince Khusrau.

s: Which pair (Guru – Mughal emperor) is correctly matched?
x: Hargobind was held in Gwalior Fort by Jahangir and freed in 1619; Ram Das was with Akbar, Arjan with Jahangir, Tegh Bahadur with Aurangzeb.

s: Who was the regent of the minor Dalip Singh?
x: Rani Jindan acted as regent for the minor Dalip Singh, who was the last ruler of Punjab before its annexation.

s: Where did Duleep Singh, the last king of the Sikh empire, die in 1893?
x: Duleep Singh, last king of the Sikh empire (1843-1849), died in Paris on 22 October 1893.

s: Who succeeded Maharaja Ranjit Singh after his death in 1839?
x: Ranjit Singh died in 1839 and was succeeded by Kharak Singh; then came Nau Nihal Singh, Sher Singh and Duleep Singh.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Guru Hargobind — compilation of Adi Granth
x: Guru Hargobind built the Akal Takht, was imprisoned at Gwalior and fought at Kartarpur. The Adi Granth was compiled by Guru Arjan Dev.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Guru Tegh Bahadur?
o: He was the ninth Sikh Guru, born Tyag Mal in 1621.
He was executed by Jahangir in 1606.
x: Execution by Jahangir in 1606 describes Guru Arjan Dev; Tegh Bahadur was executed on Aurangzeb's orders in Delhi in 1675.

s: Where was Guru Nanak born in 1469?
o: Talwandi, also known as Nankana Sahib, near the Ravi
x: Guru Nanak was born in 1469 at Talwandi, now known as Nankana Sahib, near the Ravi.

s: Which of the following was part of Guru Nanak's teachings?
o: Worship of child Krishna through Pushtimarga
x: Guru Nanak taught Nirguna devotion, Ek Onkar, Naam Simran and Sangat, rejecting the rituals of both religions.

s: What is the literal meaning of the term 'Khalsa'?
x: Khalsa means 'pure'. The Panj Pyare were baptised with sacred nectar at its founding.

s: What does the word 'Sikh' mean?
x: 'Sikh' comes from the Sanskrit 'shishya', meaning disciple; 'Khalsa' means pure.

s: By what name did Bhai Lehna, chosen by Guru Nanak as his successor, become known?
x: Guru Nanak chose Bhai Lehna as his successor, who became Guru Angad.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Guru Angad — Introduction of Gurmukhi script
Guru Amar Das — Compilation of Adi Granth
Guru Ram Das — Militarisation of the Panth
Guru Har Krishan — Foundation of Anandpur Sahib
x: Guru Angad introduced the Gurmukhi script. The other contributions belong to Guru Arjan, Guru Hargobind and Guru Tegh Bahadur respectively.

s: Anandpur Sahib was founded by which Sikh Guru?
x: Guru Tegh Bahadur founded Anandpur Sahib, also called Chak-Nanki.

s: Which Sikh Guru organised the 22 Manjis?
x: Guru Amar Das set up the 22 Manjis.

s: Which Guru finalised the Guru Granth Sahib and introduced the Five Ks?
x: Guru Gobind Singh finalised the Guru Granth Sahib and introduced the Five Ks.

s: Who was the fifth Guru of the Sikhs?
x: Guru Arjan Dev, the fifth Guru, compiled the Adi Granth in 1604.

s:
Arrange the following Sikh Gurus in chronological order:
1. Guru Hargobind
2. Guru Amar Das
3. Guru Tegh Bahadur
4. Guru Arjan Dev
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Amar Das was the 3rd Guru, Arjan Dev the 5th, Hargobind the 6th and Tegh Bahadur the 9th.

s: What was the original name of Guru Tegh Bahadur?
x: Guru Tegh Bahadur, the ninth Guru, was born Tyag Mal in Amritsar.

s: Which Sikh Guru standardised the Gurmukhi script?
x: Guru Angad (Lehna), Nanak's successor, standardised Gurmukhi and systematised the langar.

s: Who introduced the Gurmukhi script?
x: Guru Nanak used Punjabi; his successor Guru Angad introduced the Gurmukhi script.

s: Which Sikh Guru built the Akal Takht?
x: Guru Hargobind, the sixth Guru, built the Akal Takht and was imprisoned at Gwalior.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Golden Temple — Amritsar; associated with Guru Ram Das and Guru Arjan
Anandpur Sahib — founded by Guru Amar Das
Nanded — final resting place of Guru Tegh Bahadur
x: Amritsar was founded by Guru Ram Das and the Golden Temple was built by Guru Arjan. Anandpur Sahib was founded by Guru Tegh Bahadur, Nanded is associated with Guru Gobind Singh, and Sri Muktsar Sahib with the Maghi Mela.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: Nanded is associated with Guru Gobind Singh's final resting place. The Maghi Mela is held at Sri Muktsar Sahib, while Talwandi Sabo is associated with the Baisakhi fair and Anandpur Sahib with Holla Mohalla.

s: With which place is Holla Mohalla associated?
x: Holla Mohalla is held at Anandpur Sahib; Maghi Mela is at Sri Muktsar Sahib.

s: Where is the Maghi Mela held?
x: The Maghi Mela is held at Sri Muktsar Sahib; Talwandi Sabo hosts a Baisakhi fair.

s: In which year was the Adi Granth installed in the Harmandir Sahib at Amritsar?
x: Guru Arjan Dev completed and installed the Adi Granth in the Harmandir Sahib in 1604.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Baisakhi — Banda Singh Bahadur’s conquest of Sirhind
Baisakhi — foundation day of the Khalsa
Shaheedi Divas — martyrdom of Guru Tegh Bahadur
Sirhind Fateh Diwas — Banda Singh Bahadur’s conquest of Sirhind
x: Baisakhi is associated with the foundation of the Khalsa, not Banda Singh Bahadur’s conquest of Sirhind. The conquest is commemorated by Sirhind Fateh Diwas.

s: Which was the capital of Banda Singh Bahadur's Sikh state?
x: Banda Singh Bahadur's capital was Lohgarh; Anandpur Sahib was founded by Guru Tegh Bahadur.

s: Who executed Banda Bahadur at Delhi in 1716?
x: Farrukhsiyar executed Banda Bahadur at Delhi in 1716 for refusing to convert.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: 1715 — Defeat of Wazir Khan at Chappar Chiri
x: Banda Bahadur seized Samana in 1709. Chappar Chiri and the conquest of Sirhind occurred in 1710, the siege of Gurdas Nangal in 1715, and his execution in 1716.

s: Who established the first sovereign Sikh state at Sirhind in 1710?
x: Banda Bahadur established the first sovereign Sikh state at Sirhind in 1710.

s: Who commissioned Banda Bahadur at Nanded in 1708?
x: Guru Gobind Singh gave Lachhman Dev the name Banda and commissioned him at Nanded in 1708.

s: Whose names did the coins minted by Banda Bahadur bear?
o: Guru Nanak and Guru Gobind Singh
Guru Arjan and Guru Gobind Singh
x: Banda Bahadur minted coins in the names of Guru Nanak and Guru Gobind Singh.

s: What was the capital of Banda Bahadur's Sikh state?
x: After conquering Sirhind in 1710, Banda made Lohgarh his capital.

s: Which Mughal commander did Banda Bahadur defeat at Chappar Chiri in 1710?
x: In 1710 Banda Bahadur defeated Wazir Khan at Chappar Chiri and conquered Sirhind.

s: What was the combined force of the Sikh misls known as?
x: The combined force of the Sikh misls was called the Dal Khalsa. Ranjit Singh united the Sikh misls.

s: The autonomous administration established by the Khalsa after 1708 lay between which two rivers?
x: After 1708, the Khalsa established an autonomous administration in the region between the Sutlej and Jamuna.

s: After Banda Bahadur, the Khalsa organised itself into how many misls?
x: The Khalsa formed 12 misls; 22 is the number of Manjis.

s: Which of the following was NOT a Sikh misl?
x: Bhangi, Ramgarhia and Phulkian were misls; Kanphata were Nath yogis.

s: Who compiled the Adi Granth in 1604?
x: Guru Arjan compiled the Adi Granth in 1604.

s: In the Sikh marriage Anand Karaj, what are the hymns sung during the circumambulations called?
x: Anand Karaj has four circumambulations of the Granth while Lavan hymns are sung.

s: The Guru Granth Sahib is written in which script?
x: The Guru Granth Sahib is written in the Gurmukhi script.

s: In which year did Guru Arjan Dev compile the Adi Granth?
x: Guru Arjan Dev compiled the Adi Granth in 1604.

s: Which Sufi saint was a contributor to the Guru Granth Sahib?
x: Sheikh Farid, along with Namdev and Ravidas, contributed to the Guru Granth Sahib.

s: Who compiled the Adi Granth, later finalised as the Guru Granth Sahib?
x: Guru Arjan compiled the Adi Granth (APPSC 2019 named Adigranth as the Sikh scripture); Guru Gobind Singh finalised it as the Guru Granth Sahib. Guru Nanak's teachings were later compiled in it, Guru Angad introduced Gurmukhi, and Guru Tegh Bahadur's 116 hymns are included in it.

s: Whose 41 shabdas are included in the Guru Granth Sahib?
x: Ravidas has 41 shabdas; 116 hymns belong to Guru Tegh Bahadur.

s: Which Guru's 116 hymns are included in the Guru Granth Sahib?
x: Guru Tegh Bahadur's 116 hymns are in the Guru Granth Sahib.

s: Who compiled the Adi Granth (Guru Granth Sahib)?
x: Guru Arjan Dev compiled the Adi Granth and installed it at Amritsar in 1604; Guru Gobind Singh declared it the Guru in 1706.

s: Which Sikh Guru declared the Adi Granth to be the Guru?
x: Guru Gobind Singh added Guru Tegh Bahadur's hymns and declared the Granth the Guru.

s: At which places did Pedro Alvares Cabral set up Portuguese factories in India?
x: Cabral, who reached Brazil and India in 1500, set up factories at Calicut, Cannanore and Cochin on the Malabar coast.

s: In which year did Vasco da Gama make his final visit to India?
x: 1502 was his second voyage; his final visit was in 1524.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Vasco da Gama arrived in India on 20 May 1498 CE.
He arrived on the eastern coast of India.
The ruler who welcomed him was Zamorin (Samuthiri).
x: Option B is incorrect: Vasco da Gama reached Calicut on the western (Malabar) coast, not the eastern coast. He arrived on 20 May 1498 and was received by the Zamorin.

s: Who commissioned Vasco da Gama's expedition that sailed from Lisbon in July 1497?
x: King Manuel I commissioned Vasco da Gama's expedition. The fleet sailed from Lisbon on 8 July 1497.

s: Where did the Portuguese settle during Vasco da Gama's second voyage (1502), after the Zamorin refused trade?
x: The Zamorin refused trade, Calicut was occupied, and the Portuguese settled at Kochi.

s: Vasco da Gama's third voyage to India in 1524 is associated with which of the following?
o: His appointment as Viceroy and his death at Kochi
His discovery of Brazil and establishment of factories
His meeting with Jahangir at Surat
His first departure from Lisbon and rounding of the Cape
x: Vasco da Gama returned in 1524 as Viceroy and died at Kochi in the same year.

s: Which of the following pairs of contemporaries and their positions in 1498 is correctly matched?
o: Immadi Narasimha Raya — Sultan of Delhi
x: Manuel I was the ruler of Portugal in 1498. The Zamorin ruled Calicut, Sikandar Lodi ruled Delhi and Immadi Narasimha Raya was associated with Vijayanagara.

s: Who guided Vasco da Gama from the African coast to Calicut according to the account of his first voyage?
x: The trader Abdul Majid is identified as the guide who helped Vasco da Gama reach Calicut from Malindi. The name also appears in variant form as Majid or Najit in some accounts; the old identification with the Arab navigator Ahmad ibn Majid is doubted, as the pilot was a Gujarati supplied by the ruler of Malindi.

s: At which place near Calicut did Vasco da Gama land in 1498?
x: Da Gama reached Calicut on 20 May 1498, landing at Kappad near Calicut.

s: After Vasco da Gama's first voyage, the spices he brought were sold in Portugal at about how many times their cost?
x: Back in Portugal in 1499, the spices sold at 60 times the cost.

s: With how many ships did Vasco da Gama leave Lisbon on 8 July 1497?
x: He left with four ships: Sao Gabriel, Sao Rafael, Berrio and a supply ship.

s: Who ruled Delhi when Vasco da Gama reached Calicut in 1498?
x: The Delhi ruler in 1498 was Sikandar Lodi, not Ibrahim Lodi.

s: From which East African port was Vasco da Gama guided to Calicut by the trader Abdul Majid?
x: Vasco da Gama was guided from Malindi on the East African coast to Calicut by the trader Abdul Majid.

s: Who was the ruler of Vijayanagara when Vasco da Gama reached Calicut in 1498?
x: In 1498 Vijayanagara was ruled by Immadi Narasimha Raya; Krishnadeva Raya came to the throne later, in 1509.

s: Which ship carried Vasco da Gama himself on his first voyage to Calicut?
x: Vasco da Gama sailed in the Sao Gabriel; the Sao Rafael was under Paulo da Gama and the Berrio under Nicolau Coelho.

s: Who received Vasco da Gama at Calicut in 1498?
x: Vasco da Gama was received by the Zamorin of Calicut.

s: By which route did Vasco da Gama reach India?
o: Round the Cape of Good Hope
x: His route went round the Cape of Good Hope to Calicut.

s: In which year was the Danish East India Company formed?
x: The Danish company was formed in 1616; English 1600, Dutch 1602, French 1664.

s: Which company, founded in 1602, is widely called the first joint-stock company to sell shares to the public?
x: The Dutch VOC (1602) is widely called the first joint-stock company to sell shares to the public.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the European companies?
o: The English East India Company was chartered in 1600
The Dutch set up their first factory at Masulipatnam in 1605
The Danes had their base at Tranquebar
The French company was formed in 1616
x: The French company was formed in 1664; 1616 is the year of the Danish company.

s: Which European power was the first to come to India and also the last to leave?
x: The Portuguese came first (1498) and left last (Goa, 1961).

s:
Arrange the following European companies in the chronological order of their formation:
1. Dutch VOC
2. French East India Company
3. English East India Company
4. Danish East India Company
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: English 1600, Dutch 1602, Danes 1616, French 1664.

s: Which European power arrived in India next after the Portuguese?
x: After the Portuguese (1498) came the Dutch, with their factory at Masulipatnam in 1605; the English got the Surat farman only in 1613.

s: Which of the following European companies was formed first?
x: The order of formation was English (1600), Dutch (1602), Danish (1616) and French (1664).

s: Which event directly disrupted the principal overland route from Europe to India in the fifteenth century?
o: The capture of Constantinople by Ottoman Sultan Mehmed II in 1453
The signing of the Treaty of Tordesillas in 1494
The first voyage of the English East India Company in 1602
The Portuguese occupation of Calicut in 1498
x: Ottoman Sultan Mehmed II captured Constantinople in 1453, closing the main overland route through Constantinople and Central Asia to India.

s: Which of the following was NOT a major motive behind European expansion towards Asia?
o: Establishing a permanent Roman imperial administration in India
Breaking the Arab control over Asian trade
x: Spices, silk, religion, wealth, prestige, rivalry and the desire to break Arab control were stated motives. Establishing a Roman imperial administration was not one of them.

s: In which year did the Ottoman Sultan Mehmed II capture Constantinople?
x: Mehmed II took Constantinople in 1453, closing the main overland route to India; 1452 is a common wrong date.

s: Before the sea route was found, which cities mainly distributed in Europe the Asian goods brought by Arab traders?
x: The trade was controlled by Arabs, and Venice and Genoa distributed the goods in Europe.

s: Peter the Great, who said 'Bear in mind that the commerce of India is the commerce of the world', was the ruler of which country?
x: Peter the Great was the ruler of Russia; his remark stressed the value of India's trade.

s: To which century of India does Peter the Great's remark 'the commerce of India is the commerce of the world' refer?
x: The remark refers to 18th-century India.

s: Which of the following technological aids made long-distance voyages safer during the Age of Discovery?
x: The caravel and astrolabe are identified as navigational advances that made long voyages safer.

s: Who set up naval training centres in Portugal and was the first European to actively promote navigation?
x: Prince Henry 'the Navigator' of Portugal set up naval training centres.

s: What was the caravel of the Age of Discovery?
x: The caravel was a ship and the astrolabe an instrument; together they made long voyages safer.

s: Who reached the southern tip of Africa in 1488 and called it the Cape of Storms?
x: Bartholomew Dias reached the southern tip of Africa in 1488 and named it the Cape of Storms. King John II later renamed it the Cape of Good Hope.

s: Which Portuguese navigator reached Brazil and India in 1500?
x: Cabral reached Brazil and India in 1500 and set up factories at Calicut, Cannanore and Cochin.

s: Which explorer is correctly matched with the achievement associated with his expedition?
o: Christopher Columbus — reached the Americas in 1492
John Cabot — first circumnavigation of the globe
Pedro Alvares Cabral — reached North America in 1497
x: Christopher Columbus reached the Americas in 1492, referred to in the account as the West Indies. Magellan is associated with the first circumnavigation, Cabral with Brazil and India, and Cabot with North America.

s: For which country did John Cabot sail when he reached North America in 1497?
x: John Cabot sailed for England, not Portugal.

s: Who made the first circumnavigation of the globe?
x: Ferdinand Magellan, sailing for Spain, made the first circumnavigation of the globe.

s: Which country sponsored Christopher Columbus, who reached the Americas in 1492?
x: Columbus sailed for Spain; Portugal sponsored the eastern route of Dias, da Gama and Cabral.

s: Who renamed the 'Cape of Storms', reached by Dias in 1488, as the Cape of Good Hope?
x: King John II of Portugal renamed it the Cape of Good Hope.

s: Which of the following pairs about the Treaty of Tordesillas is correctly matched?
o: Lands east of the meridian – Spain
Reference point of the meridian – Cape of Good Hope
Lands west of the meridian – Portugal
x: The 1494 treaty fixed a meridian 370 leagues west of the Cape Verde Islands, with the east going to Portugal and the west to Spain.

s: The Treaty of Tordesillas (1494) drew the dividing meridian at how many leagues west of Cape Verde?
x: The Tordesillas line lay 370 leagues west of Cape Verde.

s: Which Pope issued the papal bull Inter caetera (1493), dividing new lands between Spain and Portugal?
x: Inter caetera was issued in 1493 by Pope Alexander VI.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Treaty of Tordesillas:
1. It was signed in 1494.
2. Lands east of its line went to Spain.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The treaty was signed in 1494; lands east of the line went to Portugal and west to Spain.

s: Brazil's Nelore cattle are associated with which place in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Brazil's Nelore cattle take their name from Nellore in Andhra Pradesh and make up about 80 per cent of Brazil's livestock.

s: In July 2025, India-Brazil ties dating to Cabral's arrival in Brazil in 1500 were recalled during the PM's visit for which summit?
x: The PM's July 2025 visit was for the 17th BRICS Summit.

s: With reference to Thomas Best, which one of the following is correct?
o: He represented the Danish Company at the court of Shah Jahan.
He defeated the Portuguese at Swally and obtained the Surat farman in 1613.
He was refused permission for trade under Portuguese pressure in 1608.
He secured the right to establish factories throughout the Mughal Empire in 1615.
x: Thomas Best defeated the Portuguese at Swally in 1612, and the English obtained the Surat farman in 1613.

s: What was the result of Sir Thomas Roe's mission to Jahangir in 1615?
o: The defeat of the Portuguese at Swally
The establishment of the first English factory at Machilipatnam
A formal treaty and the transfer of Bombay to the Company
Factories at Agra, Ahmedabad and Broach, though no treaty was concluded
x: Sir Thomas Roe concluded no treaty with Jahangir, but factories were established at Agra, Ahmedabad and Broach during his mission.

s: Whose court did the English traveller Ralph Fitch visit?
x: Ralph Fitch came in the 1580s, in Akbar's reign.

s: Whose envoy was Captain William Hawkins at Jahangir's court?
x: Hawkins (came 1608) was the envoy of James I.

s: Which title did Jahangir give to William Hawkins?
x: Hawkins received the title 'English Khan', though his Surat permission was withdrawn under Portuguese pressure.

s: Whose chaplain was Edward Terry at Jahangir's court?
x: Edward Terry was Sir Thomas Roe's chaplain.

s:
Arrange the following Englishmen in the chronological order of their arrival in India:
1. Sir Thomas Roe
2. William Hawkins
3. Ralph Fitch
4. Thomas Best
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Fitch came in the 1580s, Hawkins in 1608, Best in 1612 and Roe in 1615.

s: Under whose pressure did Jahangir withdraw the Surat trading permission given to William Hawkins?
x: Hawkins got permission at Surat, but Jahangir withdrew it under Portuguese pressure; Hawkins left in 1611.

s: Who granted the charter of the English East India Company on 31 December 1600?
x: Elizabeth I granted the charter, with a 15-year monopoly between the Cape of Good Hope and the Magellan Straits.

s: The farman issued by Farrukhsiyar in 1717 is associated with which concession to the English East India Company?
o: Transfer of Bombay at nominal rent
Permission to build a fort at Bhatkal
x: Farrukhsiyar’s farman of 1717 granted the English East India Company the privilege of duty-free trade in Bengal.

s: For how many years did the English Charter of 31 December 1600 give the East India Company a monopoly of East Indies trade?
x: Elizabeth I's charter gave a 15-year monopoly, later made perpetual.

s: What was the merged body formed by the rival English East India companies in the early 18th century called?
x: The rival English companies merged into the 'United Company of Merchants' in the early 18th century.

s: Which of the following statements about the transfer of Bombay is correct?
o: It was received by Charles II as the dowry of Catherine of Braganza in 1661 and transferred to the Company in 1668.
It was received by the Company as a dowry in 1668 and transferred to Charles II in 1661.
It was acquired from the Portuguese by the Company in 1600 without Crown intervention.
It was transferred to the Company in 1757 after the Battle of Plassey.
x: Bombay formed part of Catherine of Braganza’s dowry to Charles II in 1661 and was transferred by the Crown to the Company in 1668.

s: Who obtained the site for Madras from the Raja of Chandragiri and built Fort St. George in 1639?
x: Francis Day obtained the site from the Raja of Chandragiri and built Fort St. George at Madras in 1639.

s: In which year was Fort William at Calcutta built?
x: Job Charnock settled at Sutanuti in 1690, the zamindaris were bought in 1698 and Fort William was built in 1700.

s: In which year did Job Charnock settle at Sutanuti?
x: Job Charnock reached Sutanuti in 1690; Fort William followed in 1700.

s: Who issued the Golden Farman of 1632 granting English trade concessions?
x: Abdullah Qutb Shah of Golconda issued the Golden Farman (Bangaru Farmana) in 1632, granting trade concessions to the English on the Andhra coast.

s: Which three villages did the English buy in 1698 that grew into the city of Calcutta?
x: In 1698 the Company bought the zamindari of Sutanuti, Gobindapur and Kalikata; Fort William followed in 1700.

s: In which year did the English buy the zamindari of Sutanuti, Gobindapur and Kalikata?
x: Job Charnock settled at Sutanuti in 1690; the three villages were bought in 1698 and Fort William built in 1700.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Dutch East India Company?
o: The States-General granted it sovereign powers
It could wage war, build forts and conclude treaties
It was given only the right to collect customs duties in Indian ports
x: The States-General gave the VOC (1602) sovereign powers such as making war, building forts and concluding treaties, not merely a right to collect customs.

s: Which of the following was an important reason for the ultimate success of the British in India?
o: The British relied exclusively on naval power and did not use Indian alliances.
The British avoided all involvement in the internal disputes of Indian rulers.
The English East India Company was a private joint-stock company with steady finance and exploited rivalries among Indian rulers.
The English East India Company was directly financed and administered by every Indian ruler.
x: The British benefited from the steady finances of a private joint-stock company and from using the rivalries among Indian rulers.

s: What did the English Charter of 1600 give the East India Company?
x: The 1600 Charter gave exclusive trading rights, not territorial or legislative powers.

s: In which year did the French establish their first factory in India at Surat?
x: The French first factory was at Surat in 1668; the Dutch began at Masulipatnam in 1605 and the Danes at Tranquebar in 1620.

s: Where was the first Danish factory in India set up in 1620?
x: The Danes set up their first factory at Tranquebar (1620); Serampore came in 1755.

s: In which year did the Danes make Serampore their headquarters?
x: The Danes began at Tranquebar (1620) and took Serampore in Bengal as their base in 1755; they sold both to the British in 1845.

s: Who founded Pondicherry, the French headquarters, in 1674?
x: Francois Martin founded Pondicherry (1674); Caron set up the Surat factory.

s: From whom did the French buy Karaikal in 1739?
x: Karaikal was bought from the Raja of Tanjore in 1739.

s:
Consider the following statements about French settlements:
1. Masulipatnam (1669) was a grant from the Sultan of Golconda.
2. Mahe lies on the Coromandel coast.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The 1669 Masulipatnam grant came from the Sultan of Golconda; Mahe (1725) is on the Malabar coast.

s:
Arrange the following French settlements in the chronological order of their establishment:
1. Pondicherry
2. Surat
3. Mahe
4. Masulipatnam
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Surat 1668, Masulipatnam 1669, Pondicherry 1674, Mahe 1725.

s: Which French settlement was set up in 1669 on a grant from the Sultan of Golconda?
x: Masulipatnam (1669), the second French settlement, came from a Golconda grant.

s: From whom did the French get the grant for their settlement at Chandernagore?
x: Chandernagore was set up on a grant from Shaista Khan, the Mughal governor of Bengal (1673).

s: Bheemunipatnam in North Coastal Andhra was a settlement of which European power?
x: Bheemunipatnam was a Dutch settlement; Yanam was French.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: The Portuguese were called Budata Keechu by local people. Bangaru Farmana was the Golden Farman, and Pulicat became the Dutch headquarters.

s: Which French enclave lies in the Godavari delta of Andhra?
x: Yanam (1723) in the Godavari delta is one of the four French enclaves.

s: In which year was the French settlement at Yanam established?
x: Yanam dates from 1723 and was re-occupied in 1731.

s: In which year did the Danes sell Serampore and Tranquebar to the British?
x: The Danes sold both bases to the British in 1845.

s: Between whom was the Battle of Swally, near Surat in 1612, fought?
x: At Swally in 1612, the English under Thomas Best defeated the Portuguese near Surat.

s: Between whom was the Battle of Wandiwash (1760) fought?
o: The English under Eyre Coote and the French under Lally
The English under Thomas Best and the Portuguese
Travancore under Marthanda Varma and the Dutch
The English under Francis Forde and the Dutch
x: Wandiwash (1760): English (Eyre Coote) defeated French (Lally). Thomas Best vs Portuguese was Swally 1612; Marthanda Varma vs Dutch was Colachel 1741; Forde vs Dutch was Bedara 1759.

s: Whom did Marthanda Varma of Travancore defeat in the Battle of Colachel (1741)?
x: At Colachel in 1741 Travancore under Marthanda Varma beat the Dutch.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: At Bedara (1759) the English under Forde beat the Dutch; Wandiwash was against the French, Colachel was won by Travancore and Swally by the English.

s: Who commanded the English in the Battle of Bedara (1759) against the Dutch?
x: Francis Forde led the English who beat the Dutch at Bedara in 1759; Eyre Coote won at Wandiwash (1760).

s: With whose help did the English take Ormuz from the Portuguese in 1622?
x: In 1622 the English and the Shah of Persia took Ormuz from the Portuguese.

s: Who formulated the Blue Water Policy in Portuguese India?
x: Francisco de Almeida, the first Portuguese viceroy in India, followed the Blue Water Policy, which emphasised naval mastery rather than territorial expansion inland.

s: Which one of the following was NOT associated with Afonso de Albuquerque?
o: Capture of Goa from Bijapur in 1510
Transfer of the Portuguese headquarters from Cochin to Goa in 1530
Abolition of Sati in Portuguese territories
x: Nuno da Cunha moved the Portuguese headquarters from Cochin to Goa in 1530. Albuquerque captured Goa, encouraged mixed marriages and abolished Sati.

s: Which Portuguese governor reversed Almeida's naval policy and pursued territorial conquest, including Goa?
x: Albuquerque reversed Almeida's exclusively naval approach and took Goa, Malacca and Hormuz.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Blue Water Policy – Portuguese naval and trading supremacy
Alauddin's market policy – Portuguese naval supremacy
Home Rule Movement – Boycott of foreign goods
x: The Blue Water Policy sought Portuguese naval and trading supremacy; Alauddin's market policy controlled prices to maintain a large army, Swadeshi meant boycott and Home Rule sought self-government.

s: Who moved the Portuguese headquarters from Cochin to Goa in 1530?
x: Nuno da Cunha (1529-38) moved the headquarters from Cochin to Goa in 1530.

s: Which place in South-East Asia did Afonso de Albuquerque capture in 1511?
x: Albuquerque took Goa in 1510 and Malacca in 1511, and also Hormuz.

s: In which year did Albuquerque capture Malacca?
x: Albuquerque captured Malacca in 1511, a year after he took Goa from Bijapur (1510).

s: Goa, taken in 1510, was the first European territory in India since the time of which ruler?
x: Goa was the first European territory in India since Alexander.

s: Who was the first Portuguese Viceroy in India?
x: Almeida was the first Viceroy and won the Battle of Diu in 1509.

s: Who shifted the Portuguese headquarters from Cochin to Goa in 1530?
x: Nino (Nuno) da Cunha moved the headquarters to Goa in 1530.

s: Who promoted the Portuguese 'marriage policy' of mixed marriages?
x: Albuquerque, the real founder of Portuguese power, promoted mixed marriages.

s:
Consider the following statements about Afonso de Albuquerque:
1. He took Goa from Bijapur in 1510.
2. He continued Almeida's Blue Water Policy.
3. He abolished Sati in his territories.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Albuquerque took Goa (1510) and abolished Sati in his territories, but he reversed the Blue Water Policy in favour of territorial conquest.

s: Besides Goa, which places did Afonso de Albuquerque conquer?
x: Albuquerque reversed Almeida's policy and went for territory: Goa, Malacca and Hormuz.

s: Which Portuguese governor pursued territorial conquest by taking Goa, Malacca and Hormuz?
x: Albuquerque gave up Almeida's Blue Water Policy and conquered Goa, Malacca and Hormuz.

s: Whose combined fleet did Almeida defeat in the Battle of Diu (1509)?
o: Gujarat, the Egyptian Mamluks and the Zamorin
The English, the Persians and Bijapur
x: Almeida defeated the combined fleet of Gujarat, the Egyptian Mamluks and the Zamorin at Diu in 1509.

s: In which year did Albuquerque capture Goa for the Portuguese?
x: Albuquerque captured Goa in 1510; Almeida's Blue Water Policy was an earlier, separate strategy.

s: With whom is the 'Blue Water Policy' associated?
x: Francisco de Almeida followed the Blue Water Policy; Albuquerque captured Goa in 1510.

s: Which one of the following was introduced in India by the Portuguese?
x: Tobacco is one of the New World crops the Portuguese brought to India, along with potato, chilli, maize, pineapple, papaya, cashew and groundnut. Rubber, tea and coffee are not in that list.

s: Which of the following was NOT brought to India by the Portuguese?
x: The Portuguese brought tobacco, cashew and maize, but not tea, coffee or rubber.

s: In which year did the Portuguese introduce the first printing press in India at Goa?
x: The Portuguese introduced the printing press at Goa in 1556.

s: Where are the remains of St. Francis Xavier, who reached Goa in 1542, preserved?
x: Xavier's remains are at the Basilica of Bom Jesus, Goa.

s: Which of the following is NOT a New World crop brought by the Portuguese?
x: Tomato, chilli and tobacco came with the Portuguese from the New World; wheat did not.

s: The Portuguese press at Goa printed the Bible in which languages?
x: The Goa press (1556) printed the Bible in Kannada and Malayalam.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Wheat — Portuguese New World crop introduced into India
x: Tobacco, chilli and tomato (to Telugu soil) are Portuguese introductions. Wheat is the wrong pair: it is not a New World crop and is not among the crops the Portuguese introduced.

s: In which year did St. Francis Xavier reach Goa?
x: The Jesuit St. Francis Xavier reached Goa in 1542; his remains are in the Basilica of Bom Jesus.

s: In which year did the Portuguese set up the first printing press in India at Goa?
x: The printing press came to Goa in 1556. 1510 is the capture of Goa, 1542 the arrival of St. Francis Xavier, and 1661 the Bombay dowry.

s: In which year was the Portuguese first factory established at Calicut?
x: The Portuguese set up their first factory at Calicut in 1500, under Pedro Alvares Cabral. 1503 is the Cochin fort, 1534 is Chatgaon, and 1611 is the English at Masulipatnam.

s: Who built the Portuguese forts at Cannanore and Anjediva in 1505?
x: Almeida built the forts at Cannanore and Anjediva in 1505.

s: Where did the Portuguese set up their factories in Bengal in 1534?
x: In 1534 the Portuguese opened factories at Satgaon and Chatgaon (Chittagong) in Bengal.

s: The treaty negotiated by Friar Luis with Krishnadevaraya during 1509–10 was associated with which development?
o: The Portuguese acquisition of Bombay from Charles II
The Portuguese capture of Goa with assistance from Timmaju
x: Friar Luis negotiated with Krishnadevaraya, and the Vijayanagara naval commander Timmaju assisted the Portuguese in capturing Goa.

s: From whom did the Portuguese obtain Diu in 1535?
x: Diu came from Bahadur Shah of Gujarat in 1535; Goa was taken from the Bijapur Sultan in 1510.

s: In which year did the Marathas capture Salsette and Bassein from the Portuguese?
x: The Marathas took Salsette and Bassein in 1739, though the Portuguese held Goa against them in 1798.

s: Which ruler allowed Albuquerque to build a fort at Bhatkal for the horse trade?
x: Krishnadeva Raya allowed the Bhatkal fort, linked to the horse trade.

s: Which Gujarat ruler allowed Nuno da Cunha to build the Diu fort in 1535?
x: Bahadur Shah of Gujarat, pressed by Humayun, let da Cunha build the Diu fort; it was not Mahmud Begada.

s: In which year did the Portuguese gain full control of Diu by conquest?
x: Diu: 1509 battle, 1535 fort, 1546 conquest.

s: Pressed by which Mughal ruler did Bahadur Shah of Gujarat allow the Portuguese to build the Diu fort in 1535?
x: Bahadur Shah, under pressure from Humayun, let Nuno da Cunha build the Diu fort in 1535.

s: In which year did the Portuguese obtain Daman by treaty?
x: Daman was obtained in 1559; Bassein in 1534, and Diu was conquered in 1546.

s: Which Portuguese settlement was granted by Akbar in 1579?
x: Akbar granted the Portuguese permission to establish themselves at Hugli in 1579.

s: From whom did the Portuguese obtain Bassein in 1534?
x: Bassein came from Bahadur Shah of Gujarat in 1534.

s: Over whose tomb was the Portuguese church at San Thome (Mylapore), 1523, built?
x: San Thome church was built over the tomb of St. Thomas.

s: In which year was the Portuguese church at Bandel, near Hugli, built?
x: Bandel church dates from 1599; Hugli was granted in 1579 and lost in 1632.

s: Which of the following was a Portuguese fort in India?
x: Aguada in Goa was a Portuguese fort; Geldria was Dutch, Fort St. Louis French and Fort St. George English.

s: Which development most directly marked the end of the Portuguese naval monopoly in the Indian Ocean?
o: The expulsion of the Portuguese from Hooghly by Shah Jahan alone
The rise of the Dutch and English as competing maritime powers
The establishment of the French settlement at Yanam
The sale of Serampore and Tranquebar by the Danes
x: The Portuguese naval monopoly ended with the emergence of the Dutch and English as competing maritime powers.

s: In which year did Shah Jahan expel the Portuguese from Hooghly?
x: Shah Jahan drove the Portuguese out of their Bengal base at Hooghly in 1632.

s: Which Mughal emperor captured Hugli from the Portuguese in 1632?
x: Shah Jahan took Hugli in 1632; Akbar had granted it to the Portuguese in 1579.

s: Shaista Khan, Bengal governor under Aurangzeb, captured which places while suppressing the Arakanese pirates?
x: Shaista Khan captured Sondip and Chittagong and suppressed the Arakanese pirates.

s: Who was Shah Jahan's Bengal governor who defeated the Portuguese at Hugli in 1632?
x: In 1632 Qasim Khan, Shah Jahan's Bengal governor, defeated the Portuguese at Hugli.

s: Which of the following was associated with the Goa Inquisition?
o: Use of state machinery for conversions and action against religious dissent
Suppression of Arakanese piracy by Shaista Khan
Promotion of religious dissent by Portuguese officials
x: The Goa Inquisition in the sixteenth century acted against religious dissent and used state machinery for conversions.

s: Which one of the following was NOT a major factor in the decline of Portuguese power in India?
o: A sustained increase in support from the Dutch and English
The merger of Portugal with Spain in 1580
x: Dutch and English competition contributed to Portuguese decline rather than supporting Portugal. Weak successors, official corruption and the 1580 merger with Spain were among the causes of decline.

s: Which of the following territories was lost by the Portuguese to the Dutch in 1663?
x: The Portuguese lost Cochin to the Dutch in 1663. Their other losses to the Dutch were Pulicat (1610) and Nagapattinam (1658); Daman, Diu and Hugli were not lost to the Dutch (Hugli fell to Shah Jahan in 1632).

s:
Consider the following statements about Portuguese defeats by the English:
1. The Battle of Swally was fought in 1612.
2. The Portuguese lost Ormuz in 1622 to the English and the Shah of Persia.
3. The defeat off Jask came before the Battle of Swally.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Swally was in 1612 and Ormuz was lost in 1622; the defeat off Jask (1620) came after Swally, so statement 3 is wrong.

s: In which year was Portugal merged with Spain, weakening Portuguese power in India?
x: Portugal merged with Spain in 1580, a cause of Portuguese decline.

s: In which year did the Portuguese lose Nagapattinam to the Dutch?
x: Nagapattinam went to the Dutch in 1658; Pulicat in 1610 and Cochin in 1663.

s: Which of the following is true of Pulicat in the European trade network?
o: the English capital of the Madras Presidency
the French headquarters and a centre for indigo
a Portuguese settlement captured by the Dutch and later their headquarters
the Danish headquarters after the acquisition of Serampore
x: Pulicat was initially Portuguese, was captured by the Dutch and became the Dutch headquarters in 1610; pepper and cloth were important commodities there.

s: Through which operation were Goa, Daman and Diu liberated from Portuguese rule in 1961?
x: The Portuguese, first to arrive and last to leave, lost Goa, Daman and Diu in 1961 through Operation Vijay.

s: In which year did the Portuguese, the first Europeans to come to India, finally leave India?
x: The Portuguese were the last European power to leave, in 1961; 1510 is when Goa was taken.

s: What was the Portuguese state in Asia known as?
x: Their Asian state was the Estado da India, with HQ first at Cochin and later Goa.

s: On which date did Operation Vijay free Goa from Portuguese rule?
x: Operation Vijay freed Goa on 19 December 1961; statehood came in May 1987.

s: To which European power did the Portuguese lose Pulicat in 1610?
x: The Dutch took Pulicat from the Portuguese in 1610 and made it their Coromandel headquarters.

s: In which year did the Portuguese lose Pulicat to the Dutch?
x: Pulicat passed to the Dutch in 1610; Nagapattinam followed in 1658.

s: What were the Portuguese popularly called in the Telugu country?
x: Locals called the Portuguese Budata Keechu. Bangaru Farmana is the Golden Farman given to the English, Kalamkari is a painted textile, and Petapoli is another name for Nizampatnam.

s: To which European power did the Machilipatnam factory of 1669-70, allowed by Abdullah Qutb Shah, belong?
x: That factory was French, the last Europeans in Andhra, not Portuguese.

s: Which of the following pairs about European activity on the Andhra coast is correctly matched?
o: French factory at Machilipatnam (1669-70) – Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah
Cause of Portuguese decline – Religious tolerance
Waning of Portuguese influence – Early 16th century
French factory at Machilipatnam (1669-70) – Abdullah Qutb Shah
x: The French factory at Machilipatnam (1669-70) was permitted by Abdullah Qutb Shah. Portuguese influence waned by the mid-17th century because their religious intolerance alienated Golconda.

s: Which Andhra port was known as Petapoli?
x: Petapoli was the old name used by Europeans for Nizampatnam on the Andhra coast.

s: When did Goa attain statehood?
x: Goa became a state in May 1987; Portuguese rule had ended earlier with Operation Vijay on 19 December 1961.

s: The Portuguese cartaz system was a system of which of the following?
x: Cartaz was a naval-pass system used to regulate shipping and enforce the Portuguese maritime monopoly, along with convoys and customs duties.

s: What mainly caused the constant conflict between the Portuguese and the Zamorin of Calicut?
o: Alliance with the Arakanese pirates against Calicut
x: The Portuguese monopoly over trade and their heavy duties led to continuing conflict with the Zamorin of Calicut.

s: What was the convoy system that backed the Portuguese Cartaz system called?
x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (Cafila); it is added as option 5.
The convoy of local merchant ships sailing under a Portuguese naval escort, which backed the cartaz, was the cafila. 'Caes' is not the term; Feitoria means a factory, Padroado the Crown's church patronage, and Estado the Portuguese state.

s: What does the term 'Cartaz' refer to in the context of Portuguese rule in India?
o: A naval trade licence or pass
x: A Cartaz was a Portuguese naval trade licence or pass required for ships sailing in the Indian Ocean.

s: Under the Cartaz system, what happened to a ship found sailing without a pass?
o: Let go after paying a fine
x: A ship without a Cartaz was confiscated or sunk.

s: Which was the Europeans' first port in Andhra?
x: Machilipatnam was the Europeans' first Andhra port; the Dutch set up their first factory in India there in 1605.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Pulicat became the Dutch headquarters in 1610, later being replaced by Nagapatnam. The French headquarters was Pondicherry, while Tranquebar was the initial Danish headquarters.

s: Which European power established the first European factory in Andhra, and where?
x: The APPSC key identifies the Portuguese as the founders of the first European factory in Andhra at Machilipatnam. Other accounts identify a Dutch factory at Masulipatnam in 1605, so the examination convention must be noted.

s: With whose permission did the Dutch settle at Pulicat?
x: Pulicat was granted by the Chandragiri king; Golconda gave Machilipatnam. Fort Geldria at Pulicat was the Coromandel headquarters till 1690.

s: Who set up the first Dutch factory in Andhra, at Machilipatnam in 1605?
x: Van der Haghen set up the Machilipatnam factory in 1605 with permission from Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah.

s: Which European power had traded at Machilipatnam before the establishment of the first Dutch factory there?
x: The Portuguese had traded at Machilipatnam before the Dutch established their factory there.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
x: Nizampatnam was a Krishna delta weaving centre, not the Dutch headquarters. Pulicat was the headquarters until 1690.

s: In which year did the Dutch set up their factory at Bheemunipatnam?
x: Bheemunipatnam was founded in 1641; Palakollu came in 1652, Pulicat in 1610, Machilipatnam in 1605.

s: In which delta was Palakollu (Palicol), a Dutch factory of 1652, a weaving centre?
x: Palakollu was a Godavari delta weaving centre; Nizampatnam (Petapuli) was the Krishna delta centre.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Dutch in Andhra:
1. Pulicat was the Dutch Coromandel headquarters till 1690.
2. Nizampatnam was the Dutch headquarters on the Coromandel coast.
3. Fort Geldria was built at Pulicat.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Pulicat with Fort Geldria was the HQ till 1690; Nizampatnam was only a Krishna delta weaving centre, not the HQ.

s:
Match the following Dutch factories in Andhra with the year of their founding:
List-I
A. Machilipatnam
B. Pulicat
C. Bheemunipatnam
D. Palakollu
List-II
1. 1641
2. 1605
3. 1652
4. 1610
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Machilipatnam 1605, Pulicat 1610, Bheemunipatnam 1641, Palakollu 1652.

s: Which of the following Dutch factories in Andhra was founded last?
x: Palakollu (1652) came after Machilipatnam (1605), Pulicat (1610) and Bheemunipatnam (1641).

s: Which Golconda ruler permitted the Dutch factory at Machilipatnam in 1605?
x: The Dutch set up their Machilipatnam factory in 1605 with the permission of Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah of Golconda.

s: Which Dutch factory of 1606 in the Krishna delta was also called Petapuli?
x: Petapuli (Nizampatnam), set up in 1606, was a Krishna delta weaving centre; Palakollu was in the Godavari delta.

s: From whom did the Dutch take Nagapattinam in 1658?
x: Nagapattinam was taken by the Dutch from the Portuguese in 1658 and later became their chief factory.

s: Nagapattinam became the chief Dutch factory after the decline of which centre in 1690?
x: Pulicat was the chief Dutch centre until 1690, after which Nagapattinam became the chief factory.

s: Which statement regarding the Dutch establishment at Cochin is correct?
o: It was founded by the Dutch in 1605 and abandoned in 1690.
It was taken from Travancore in 1741 and returned to Portugal in 1824.
It was taken from the Portuguese in 1663 and passed to the British in 1795.
It was taken from the English in 1663 and ceded to the French in 1795.
x: The Dutch took Cochin from the Portuguese in 1663; it later passed to the British in 1795.

s: In which year did Cochin, taken by the Dutch from the Portuguese in 1663, pass to the British?
x: Cochin (Dutch from 1663) passed to the British in 1795; 1824 is the Anglo-Dutch Treaty.

s: Which Dutch factory was established in 1645?
x: Karaikal came in 1645, after Surat (1616) and before Chinsura (1653) and Nagapattinam (1658).

s: Mahe was a centre of which European power?
x: Mahe was a French centre; Kasimbazar, Balasore and Vengurla were Dutch.

s: Where was the first Dutch factory in Bengal?
x: The Dutch first set up in Bengal at Pipali (1627), later Balasore; Chinsura came in 1653.

s: In which year did the Dutch set up their factory at Surat?
x: The Dutch factory at Surat came in 1616, after the English one (1613).

s: Whom did Travancore under Marthanda Varma defeat at the Battle of Colachel (1741)?
x: Travancore defeated the Dutch at Colachel in 1741, ending Dutch ambitions in Malabar.

s: Who was the English commander who defeated the Dutch in the Battle of Bedara (1759)?
x: Francis Forde led the English at Bedara; J.B. Russell led the Dutch.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Bedara – ended Dutch ambitions in Malabar
x: Colachel (1741) was won by Marthanda Varma of Travancore; Bedara (1759) was English vs Dutch.

s: Which of the following pairs about the Battle of Bedara (Chinsura) is correctly matched?
o: Result – Dutch moved headquarters to Chinsura
x: At Bedara in 1759 the English under Francis Forde (with Clive directing) defeated the Dutch, who then withdrew to Indonesia. Eyre Coote won Wandiwash (1760).

s: Which battle ended Dutch ambitions in Malabar?
x: At Colachel (1741) Marthanda Varma of Travancore beat the Dutch, ending their ambitions in Malabar.

s: Which of the following was a major reason for the decline of Dutch power in India?
o: Their Coromandel cloth trade was always more profitable than Indonesian spices.
They were supported by the English against all Indian powers.
They completely abandoned maritime trade after 1605.
Their priority was the Indonesian spice monopoly rather than Indian territorial expansion.
x: The Dutch prioritised their spice monopoly in Indonesia, while Malabar was less profitable to them than the Coromandel cloth trade. This weakened their long-term commitment to India.

s: In which year was the Anglo-Dutch Treaty, under which the Dutch ceded Pulicat, signed?
x: Pulicat was ceded under the Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824; the Dutch occupation is dated 1605-1825.

s: In which years were the Anglo-Dutch conferences that failed to end English-Dutch rivalry held?
x: The Anglo-Dutch conferences of 1613 and 1615 failed, adding to English rivalry.

s: Which of the following is NOT a cause of the decline of the Dutch in India?
o: Their priority on Indian territory over the Indonesian spice monopoly
Loss of Andhra strongholds in the Anglo-French wars
x: The Dutch put the Indonesian spice monopoly first, not Indian territory.

s: When was the Vereenigde Oostindische Compagnie (VOC) formed?
x: The VOC was formed on 20 March 1602 by merging Dutch companies. The year 1592 is a commonly noted misprint.

s: From whom did the VOC receive sovereign powers to wage war, build forts and sign treaties?
x: The Dutch States-General granted the VOC powers to wage war, build forts and sign treaties.

s: What was the headquarters of the VOC in Asia?
x: Batavia, now Jakarta, was the Asian headquarters of the VOC.

s: Who wrote the Itinerario, part of the background to Dutch expansion in Asia?
x: Linschoten wrote the Itinerario, while Cornelis de Houtman reached Bantam in 1596.

s: Who reached Bantam in 1596, opening the Dutch route to Asia?
x: Cornelis de Houtman reached Bantam in 1596; Linschoten wrote the Itinerario.

s: Whose ban on Lisbon pushed the Dutch to sail directly to Asia?
x: Philip II's ban on Dutch trade at Lisbon pushed the Dutch to find their own sea route to Asia.

s: The Dutch were the first European traders in Andhra to obtain the right to do which of the following?
o: Issue farmans in their own name
x: The Dutch were the first to obtain the right to mint coins in Andhra.

s: Which of the following commodities was imported into the Coromandel ports by the Dutch?
x: Silk and porcelain were imported, whereas gems, diamonds, indigo, cotton, Kalamkari and cloth were among the exports.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
x: Pulicat was a hub of the slave trade to Batavia, not a centre of porcelain production. Koringa was associated with shipbuilding and Chittavalasa with jute.

s: What was Pulicat a hub of under the Dutch?
x: Pulicat was a hub of the slave trade to Batavia, not of porcelain.

s: From which region did saltpetre mainly come in the Dutch carrying trade?
x: Saltpetre came from Bihar; pepper came from Malabar.

s: What was Koringa in Andhra known for under the Dutch?
x: Koringa was a Dutch shipbuilding centre; jute was at Chittavalasa.

s: Between which places did the Dutch Andhra network broadly extend?
x: The Dutch network in Andhra ran from Machilipatnam to Bheemunipatnam, along the coast.

s: Where did Fort Geldria, the only Dutch fortification in India, stand?
x: Fort Geldria at Pulicat was the Dutch's only fort in India; Bheemunipatnam has the Dutch cemetery.

s: Which place in Andhra Pradesh has a Dutch cemetery, a remain of the Dutch factory of 1641?
x: Bheemunipatnam (1641) is known for its Dutch cemetery.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Fort Geldria?
o: It was the only Dutch fortification in India
It was blown up by the British in 1804
x: Fort Geldria was at Pulicat, not Bheemunipatnam, which is known for its Dutch cemetery.

s:
Consider the following statements about the English East India Company:
1. It was formed during the reign of Akbar.
2. Its first factories in India came up during the reign of Jahangir.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Company was formed in 1600 under Akbar; its first factories (1611, 1613) came under Jahangir.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Ralph Fitch was the first English merchant to visit Akbar's court.
Ralph Fitch visited Agra and Fatehpur Sikri.
x: Option C is incorrect: Ralph Fitch was in India from 1583 to 1586, not 1586 to 1589. He visited Agra and Fatehpur Sikri and was the first English merchant at Akbar's court.

s: Whose ambassador was Sir Thomas Roe when he came to Jahangir's court in 1615?
x: James I sent both Hawkins and Roe to Jahangir.

s: Who was Edward Terry at Jahangir's court?
x: Edward Terry was Roe's chaplain; Hippon captained the Globe and Surman led the 1717 mission.

s: Who was the first envoy of James I to reach Jahangir's court?
x: Hawkins reached Jahangir's court at Agra in 1609; Roe came later in 1615.

s: Who defeated the Portuguese in the Battle of Swally (1612)?
x: Captain Thomas Best of the English East India Company defeated the Portuguese at Swally near Surat in 1612, winning the English a factory at Surat.

s: For how many years did the 1600 charter first give the English East India Company a monopoly of East Indies trade?
x: The charter gave a fifteen-year monopoly, later made perpetual; it granted trading rights, not territorial power.

s: What was the internal organisation of the early English East India Company?
o: A Governor and a 24-member committee, with shareholders forming the General Court
A President and a 40-member committee, with merchants forming the Royal Court
A Governor and a 12-member committee, with the Crown forming the General Court
A Viceroy and a 24-member committee, with Parliament forming the General Court
x: The Company was run by a Governor and a 24-member committee, later known as the Court of Directors. Shareholders constituted the General Court, or Court of Proprietors.

s: Charles II and James II delegated to the Company the powers of coining money and exercising jurisdiction. Which other power did they delegate?
o: declaring war and peace with non-Christians
x: The delegated powers included coining money, jurisdiction and making war and peace with non-Christians.

s: From whom did the English East India Company receive its charter on 31 December 1600?
x: Queen Elizabeth I granted the charter on 31 December 1600. James I sent Hawkins and Roe to Jahangir, Charles II received Bombay as dowry and delegated sovereign powers, and Cromwell gave the 1657 charter for a permanent joint stock.

s: With what did the English East India Company largely pay for Indian goods during its early trade?
x: Imported bullion was used to pay for Indian goods in the early period of Company trade.

s: What was the early objective of the East India Company?
o: Eastern trade, especially spices and textiles
x: The Company's early objective was eastern trade, especially in spices and textiles. Territorial rule over Bengal came only after 1757.

s: Who led the English East India Company's first voyage in 1602?
x: James Lancaster led the first voyage in 1602 with £68,000 capital, setting up a factory at Bantam.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Charter of 1600?
o: It was granted by Elizabeth I
It gave a 15-year monopoly of East Indies trade
It gave territorial governance and legislative power
x: The 1600 Charter gave trading rights only, not territorial or legislative power (APPSC-GS 2024).

s: On which date did Queen Elizabeth I grant the royal charter to the English East India Company?
x: The charter was granted on 31 December 1600; 20 March 1602 is the date of the Dutch VOC.

s: In which year did Oliver Cromwell's charter give the English East India Company a permanent joint stock?
x: Cromwell's charter of 1657 made the joint stock permanent.

s: What was the official name of the English East India Company under the charter of 1600?
o: The Governor and Company of Merchants of London Trading into the East Indies
The United Company of Merchants of England Trading to the East Indies
x: The 1600 charter named it 'The Governor and Company of Merchants of London Trading into the East Indies'.

s:
Consider the following statements about the English East India Company:
1. Its official name was 'The Governor and Company of Merchants of London Trading into the East Indies'.
2. It was formed by a group called the 'Merchant Adventurers'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: the Merchant Adventurers (c.1599) formed the company, chartered under that official name.

s: Between which limits did the charter of 1600 give the English East India Company its trade monopoly?
o: Cape of Good Hope and the Straits of Magellan
Gibraltar and the Cape of Good Hope
Red Sea and the Persian Gulf
x: The 1600 charter gave a 15-year monopoly of trade between the Cape of Good Hope and the Straits of Magellan.

s: Where did the first voyage of the English East India Company (1602) under James Lancaster set up a factory?
x: James Lancaster's first voyage of 1602 set up a factory at Bantam in Java.

s: In which year was the Levant Company, the first British company chartered to trade with the Ottoman Empire and the East, set up?
x: The Levant Company was chartered in 1592, eight years before the East India Company (1600).

s: Which Act ended the rule of the English East India Company in India?
x: The Government of India Act, 1858 ended Company rule and the Crown took over.

s: Who founded Madras, including Fort St. George, in 1639, and on whose grant?
o: Francis Day after obtaining a grant from Venkatapati Raya III
Job Charnock after a grant from Aurangzeb
Thomas Best after obtaining a farman from Jahangir
Anthony Hippon after obtaining permission from Abdullah Qutb Shah
x: Francis Day founded Madras in 1639 after obtaining a grant from the Chandragiri ruler Venkatapati Raya III, with the efforts of the Damerla brothers, Venkatadri and Ayyappa.

s: Which Chandragiri ruler granted the land for Madras in 1639?
x: Venkatapati Raya III of Chandragiri gave the grant, with efforts of the Damerla brothers.

s: In which year was Fort St. George completed on St George's Day, 23 April?
x: Begun in 1639-40, Fort St. George was completed on 23 April 1644.

s:
Consider the following statements about the founding of Madras:
1. Francis Day founded it with Andrew Cogan.
2. The Damerla brothers helped obtain the grant.
3. Madras became India's first municipality in 1861.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Madras was founded in 1639 by Francis Day and Andrew Cogan with the Damerla brothers' help; it became a municipality in 1687 (Bhimili was Andhra's first in 1861).

s: Which English Presidency seat was at Fort St. George?
x: Madras was at Fort St. George and Calcutta at Fort William in Bengal; Bombay replaced Surat in the west.

s: In which year did Madras become the first municipality in India?
x: Madras was India's first municipality in 1687; Bhimili was Andhra's first in 1861.

s: On which coast were the English factories at Hariharpur and Balasore (1633)?
x: Hariharpur and Balasore (1633) were on the Odisha coast.

s: In which year was the first English factory in Bengal set up at Hugli?
x: The English set up their first Bengal factory at Hugli in 1651; Calcutta came in 1690.

s: On whose farman did the English set up their first factory in Bengal at Hugli in 1651?
x: The Hugli factory (1651) was set up on Shah Shuja's farman.

s: The zamindari of which group of villages was acquired by the East India Company in 1698, forming the basis of Calcutta?
x: In 1698, the Company bought the zamindari rights of Sutanuti, Gobindapur and Kalikata.

s: Sutanuti, one of the three villages that became Calcutta, was a trading centre of which European power?
x: Sutanuti was an English trading centre and a Calcutta base; Batavia was the Dutch eastern centre.

s: Before founding Calcutta, Job Charnock was chief of which factory?
x: Job Charnock, chief of the Qasim Bazar factory, chose Sutanuti and arrived in 1690.

s: In which year was Fort William, the nucleus of Calcutta, built?
x: Charnock arrived in 1690, the villages were bought in 1698 and Fort William came in 1700.

s: Who leased Bombay to the English East India Company in 1668?
x: Charles II leased Bombay to the Company in 1668; Francis Day founded Madras in 1639.

s: For what annual rent was Bombay handed over to the East India Company by the English Crown in 1668?
x: In 1668, Bombay was transferred to the East India Company for an annual rent of £10.
